excerpt: On the morning of August 9, 1995, a sixteen-month-old company with no profits sold itself to the public. Netscape's bankers had priced the stock at $28. It touched $75 by the afternoon. Jim Clark, its co-founder, became the first internet paper-billionaire before the market closed, and somewhere in the building a browser engineer realized the product had become a footnote to its own ticker. Nothing about the software changed that day. Everything about the Valley did.
title: The landlords won
